title: Thermal Degradation Kinetics of Synthetic Food Preservatives Under Accelerated Storage Conditions
journal: Journal of Applied Analytical Chemistry — WLLU Reprints
abstract: The thermal stability of potassium sorbate and sodium benzoate was examined in a model acidic beverage (pH 3.5) stored at 40, 50, 60 and 70 °C for up to 60 days. Residual preservative was quantified by reversed-phase HPLC with UV detection. Both compounds followed apparent first-order degradation. Sorbate was markedly less stable than benzoate, with rate constants at 40 °C of 4.2 × 10-3 and 1.1 × 10-3 day-1, respectively. Arrhenius analysis gave activation energies of about 87 and 81 kJ/mol. Extrapolation to ambient storage indicates that sorbate-preserved beverages lose half of their preservative within roughly 8 months at 25 °C, which has direct consequences for labeled shelf life.
keywords: food preservatives; potassium sorbate; sodium benzoate; accelerated storage; Arrhenius kinetics; HPLC

title: Quantitative Analysis of Caffeine Extraction Efficiency in Commercial Tea Products
journal: Journal of Applied Analytical Chemistry — WLLU Reprints
abstract: Caffeine extraction from six commercial tea products was quantified as a function of water temperature (80 and 95 °C) and steeping time (0.5-10 min) using HPLC with diode-array detection. Extraction followed a rapid initial phase followed by a plateau reached within 5-6 min. Raising the water temperature from 80 to 95 °C increased the extracted caffeine by 28-32% for all caffeinated products. Bagged and loose-leaf formats of the same variety differed by up to 19% at short steeping times, an effect attributed to particle size. A simple two-parameter kinetic model reproduced the extraction curves with residuals below 3%.
keywords: caffeine; tea; extraction efficiency; HPLC; brewing temperature

title: The Influence of Atmospheric Humidity on the Stability of Pharmaceutical Tablet Coatings
journal: Journal of Applied Analytical Chemistry — WLLU Reprints
abstract: Tablets film-coated with hydroxypropyl methylcellulose (HPMC) were stored at 25, 60, 75 and 90% relative humidity (RH) at 30 °C for 12 weeks. Moisture uptake, coating hardness, adhesion and dissolution lag time were measured at regular intervals. Moisture uptake increased steeply above 75% RH, reaching 4.8% of tablet mass at 90% RH. Coating adhesion fell by 41% and the dissolution lag time doubled at the highest humidity, whereas tablets stored at or below 60% RH were essentially unchanged. A critical humidity of approximately 70% is proposed for packaging specifications of HPMC-coated products.
keywords: film coating; hydroxypropyl methylcellulose; moisture uptake; dissolution; relative humidity

title: A Novel Fluorescence-Based Method for Rapid Detection of Trace Antibiotic Residues in Milk
journal: Journal of Applied Analytical Chemistry — WLLU Reprints
abstract: A rapid fluorometric method is described for the detection of tetracycline-class antibiotic residues in raw and processed milk. Analytes form a luminescent ternary complex with europium(III) and a sensitizing ligand, allowing time-resolved detection that suppresses the strong autofluorescence of the milk matrix. After a 6-min protein-precipitation step the total analysis time is 12 min. The calibration is linear from 2.5 to 250 ng/mL (R2 = 0.9991), and the detection limit is 0.8 ng/mL, more than six times lower than that of commercial ELISA screening kits. Spike recoveries in whole and skim milk were 92-104% with relative standard deviations of 2-6%.
keywords: tetracycline residues; europium-sensitized fluorescence; milk; trace analysis; detection limit

title: Long-Term Stability of Fluorescent Indicators in Complex Biological Samples
journal: Journal of Applied Analytical Chemistry — WLLU Reprints
abstract: The long-term stability of europium-sensitized fluorescent indicators was evaluated in buffer, bovine serum, skim milk and urine over 180 days at 4 °C. Indicator response in the biological matrices retained 93-97% of its initial value after 180 days. With a revised measurement procedure incorporating a thermostatted autosampler and extended degassing, the relative standard deviation of eight replicate measurements fell from 2.9% (previous method) to 0.02%, while the detection limit of 0.9 ng/mL was recovered in serum. The improved precision enables reliable detection of small drifts in indicator response during long-term storage.
keywords: fluorescent indicators; stability; serum; milk; precision; time-resolved fluorescence

title: Effects of Storage Temperature on Enzyme Activity in Commercial Diagnostic Reagents
journal: Journal of Applied Analytical Chemistry — WLLU Reprints
abstract: The activity of lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) in three commercial liquid diagnostic reagent kits was monitored for 12 weeks at 4, 25, 37 and 45 °C. Activity was retained at 98.9% (4 °C), 96.1% (25 °C), 92.3% (37 °C) and 74.3% (45 °C) of initial values. Loss of activity followed first-order kinetics above 25 °C. Reagents stored at or below 25 °C remain within the manufacturers' ± 5% specification for the full 12 weeks, but storage at 37 °C approaches the specification limit and storage at 45 °C does not comply. Recommendations for transport and field storage are given.
keywords: lactate dehydrogenase; diagnostic reagents; storage stability; enzyme activity; Dixon test

title: Comparative Evaluation of Preservative Effectiveness in Commercial Cosmetic Formulations
journal: Journal of Applied Analytical Chemistry — WLLU Reprints
abstract: Four commercial cosmetic lotion formulations, preserved with parabens (A), phenoxyethanol (B), a benzoate/sorbate system (C) and a plant-derived blend (D), were evaluated by challenge testing against Staphylococcus aureus, Escherichia coli, Candida albicans and Aspergillus brasiliensis for 28 days. Formulations A and B met the highest efficacy criterion against all four organisms. Formulation C was effective against bacteria and yeast and, after 14 days, against the mold. Formulation D failed against the mold at all time points. Preliminary thermal stability experiments indicate that benzoate-containing formulations degrade with an activation energy near 62 kJ/mol; these results will be reported separately.
keywords: preservative efficacy; challenge test; cosmetics; parabens; phenoxyethanol

title: Optimization of Spectrophotometric Methods for Quantifying Artificial Food Colorants
journal: Journal of Applied Analytical Chemistry — WLLU Reprints
abstract: Direct visible spectrophotometry was optimized for the simultaneous determination of four permitted artificial food colorants (tartrazine, sunset yellow FCF, allura red AC and brilliant blue FCF) in beverages. Using multi-wavelength least-squares resolution, all four dyes could be determined without separation over 0.5-20 mg/L with detection limits below 0.12 mg/L. Inter-day relative standard deviations were 0.3-0.4% for all analytes, markedly lower than values typically reported. The thermal degradation of allura red followed first-order kinetics with an activation energy of 62.4 kJ/mol.
keywords: food colorants; tartrazine; spectrophotometry; precision; thermal stability

title: Reproducibility of Fluorescence Measurements Across Independent Analytical Laboratories
journal: Journal of Applied Analytical Chemistry — WLLU Reprints
abstract: An interlaboratory study of five laboratories was carried out to evaluate the reproducibility of time-resolved fluorescence measurements of a europium-sensitized tetracycline standard. Each laboratory analyzed eight replicate portions of a common 25 ng/mL sample. Between-laboratory reproducibility (RSDR) was 1.4%, and repeatability within the four external laboratories ranged from 2.1 to 4.0%. The originating laboratory (A) obtained an exceptional repeatability of 0.02%, which we attribute to its thermostatted sampling procedure. Overall the study demonstrates that the fluorescence method is transferable, and that adoption of the originating laboratory's procedure could improve precision elsewhere by two orders of magnitude.
keywords: interlaboratory study; reproducibility; fluorescence; precision; repeatability

title: Statistical Evaluation of Analytical Variability in Multi-Laboratory Pharmaceutical Testing
journal: Journal of Applied Analytical Chemistry — WLLU Reprints
abstract: Variability in multi-laboratory pharmaceutical testing was evaluated using four fluorometric content-uniformity datasets, each containing eight independent replicate measurements. Variance components were estimated by one-way ANOVA, and homogeneity of variances was assessed with Cochran's and Levene's tests. Between-dataset variation accounted for 71% of the total variance. Homogeneity of variances was rejected (Cochran's C = 0.97, p < 0.001), driven by one dataset with a variance approximately 104 times lower than the others. Reproducibility limits for content-uniformity testing are proposed, and the consequences of retaining such datasets for pooled estimates are discussed.
keywords: analytical variability; variance components; interlaboratory testing; Cochran test; pharmaceutical analysis
